questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: Yarrow Company reports sales of $11,850 and total variable expenses of $12,800. What is the contribution margin?

options.misconception: adds variable costs to sales instead of subtracting them
reverses the subtraction of variable costs
reports sales as if there were no variable costs

questions.explanation: Contribution margin is sales minus the variable costs that change with volume, so $11,850 less $12,800 equals $-950. This amount is available to cover fixed costs and then generate profit, so ignoring variable costs would overstate the contribution.
questions.hint: Subtract variable costs from sales, not fixed costs.

provenance.author: bank-team-acct
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: Yarrow Works has fixed costs of $11,500 and a contribution margin of $14 per unit. How many units must be sold to break even, rounded up to the nearest whole unit?

options.misconception: multiplies fixed costs by the contribution margin
inverts the break-even formula
subtracts the margin from fixed costs

questions.explanation: At break-even, total contribution equals fixed costs, so required units are $11,500 divided by $14 per unit, which rounds up to 822 whole units. Multiplying or subtracting would not give the volume at which profit is zero.
questions.hint: Divide fixed costs by contribution per unit.

questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: Ashford Supply has fixed costs of $11,150 and a contribution margin ratio of 40 percent. What sales level is required to break even?

options.misconception: uses the complement of the contribution margin ratio
multiplies fixed costs by the margin ratio rather than dividing
treats fixed costs as the break-even sales amount

questions.explanation: Break-even sales in dollars equal fixed costs divided by the contribution margin ratio, so $11,150 over forty percent gives $27,875. Multiplying by the ratio or using its complement would not identify the sales that cover all costs.
questions.hint: Divide fixed costs by the contribution margin ratio.
